english.title: Inspector disclose information re a trade secret / manufacturing process obtained by virtue of these regulations
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed information which related to a

(A)_[trade secret]_
(B)_[secret manufacturing process]_

and was obtained by you by virtue of the Weights and Measures (Packaged Goods) Regulations 2006 when you were

(C)_[an inspector,]_
(D)_[a person accompanying an inspector by virtue of paragraph 3 of Schedule 7 to those regulations,]_

the disclosure not being made in the performance of your duty as

(E)_[an inspector]_
(F)_[a person accompanying an inspector]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 16(1) and 18(3) of the Weights and Measures (Packaged Goods) Regulations 2006.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
It shall not be an offence under regulation 16(1) for a person to disclose information in circumstances where -
(a) the person from whom the public authority received the information has consented to its disclosure; or
(b) the information is disclosed more than 50 years after it was received by the public authority

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
